trial.title: Title: A Multimodal Exercise Program With Gamification for Parkinson Disease (MEP+G)

endpoints.description: Participants completing exercises as prescribed: measured using the daily exercise plan as a "yes" or "no".
Measured by daily exercise plan; instructors will indicate whether participant was present as a "yes" or "no"
Retention: number of participants who completed the entire program divided by total number who started; x 100 to determine the percentage of participants who completed the program.
Data collection: measured using a pre-populated form and marked as a "yes" or "no" by the PI.
Adverse events (i.e., falls): measured by the daily exercise plan as indicated by a numeric number and type of adverse event

Measured via Qualtrics survey asking participants "How satisfied were you in participating in this study" using an ordinal scale (0-4): (4)(strongly agree; (3)agree; (2)neutral; (1)disagree; (0)strongly disagree); with a higher score reflection increased satisfaction
Measured via using the Mini Balance Evaluation System Test (Mini-BESTest): a series of subtests with a total score from 0-28 points; with a higher score indicating improved balance.
Measured via Functional Gait Assessment (FGA): series of subtests based out of score from 0- 30 points; with a higher score indicating improved postural stability while walking.
Measured via International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ) based on minutes exercise per week with a higher number of minutes indicating increased physical activity
Gait speed measured via 10 meters divided by number of seconds to determine gait speed of meters per second (m/s); a increased in m/s indicating improved gait speed.
Functional strength measured by number of seconds required to perform 5 sit to stands (5TSTS) with a decrease in time indicating improved functional strength.
Cardiovascular endurance measured by total number of feet walked within a 6 minute timeframe (6MWT); an increase number of steps indicating improved cardiovascular endurance.

Quality of life measured by Parkinson Disease Questionnaire: 39 (PDQ39) questions asking participants to rate various aspects of their condition using an ordinal scale: 0-4 (4)(Always, (3)Often, (2)Occasionally, (1)Sometimes, (0)Never; with a higher score indicating an increased quality of life

Disease severity measured by the Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson DiseaseRating (MDS UPDRS); 18 items measured using an ordinal scale (0-4).0=none;1=slight;2=minimal;3; moderate;4=severe; with a lower score indicating less severity

outcome.rationale: Pilot study focused on feasibility endpoints with high likelihood of success given supervised structure and motivated PD population. Efficacy endpoints expected to show positive trends though underpowered for definitive efficacy. Gamification element enhances engagement and adherence.

value.uncertainty: Pilot studies typically achieve high fidelity with supervised PT-led sessions; lack of direct gamification fidelity data increases uncertainty.
value.rationale: Supervised PT-led exercise programs in PD typically achieve 85-95% fidelity. Gamification element likely enhances engagement.

value.uncertainty: Based on similar PD exercise pilots showing 80-90% adherence over 6-8 weeks.
value.rationale: Structured supervised exercise with waitlist control design motivates high attendance. Three sessions weekly for 6 weeks is feasible for motivated PD patients.

value.uncertainty: 21-month timeframe for retention assessment extends beyond 6-week intervention; may include long-term follow-up losses.
value.rationale: PD exercise pilots typically achieve 75-85% retention over 6 weeks. Extended 21-month timeframe may reduce observed retention due to attrition.

value.uncertainty: Pre-populated forms and PI oversight suggest high completeness; pilot nature emphasizes data quality.
value.rationale: Pre-populated forms with PI oversight in pilot studies typically achieve >90% data completeness. Study design emphasizes feasibility assessment.

value.uncertainty: Falls expected in balance-challenged PD population but serious adverse events rare in supervised non-contact boxing.
value.rationale: Supervised non-contact boxing for PD typically reports minimal serious adverse events. Some falls expected given balance deficits but incidence low with PT supervision.

value.uncertainty: Gamified exercise typically shows high satisfaction in PD; limited direct data for SMARTfit specifically.
value.rationale: Gamified exercise interventions in PD consistently show high participant satisfaction (mean 3-4/4). Novelty and engagement elements support positive perception.

value.estimand: experimental group change from baseline to 6 weeks
value.uncertainty: MCID for Mini-BESTest in PD is 3.4-4.0; small sample pilot may not achieve statistical significance but likely achieves clinical significance.
value.rationale: Multimodal exercise with balance training in PD typically improves Mini-BESTest by 2-5 points. MCID is 3.4-4.0 points.

value.estimand: experimental group change from baseline to 6 weeks
value.uncertainty: FGA responds to gait training; 6-week intervention may show modest gains but ceiling effects possible in mild PD (H&Y 1-3).
value.rationale: Gait-specific training including boxing footwork improves FGA scores in PD. Typical improvements 2-4 points over 6-12 weeks.

value.uncertainty: Structured 180 min/week intervention plus potential carry-over effects; self-report IPAQ may overestimate.
value.rationale: Intervention provides 180 min/week supervised exercise. IPAQ typically shows increased self-reported activity in exercise groups vs controls.

value.estimand: experimental group change from baseline to 6 weeks
value.uncertainty: Small sample pilot may lack power for significant change; gait speed responds to aerobic and resistance training.
value.rationale: Multimodal exercise in PD typically improves gait speed by 0.1-0.2 m/s. PMC3263544 showed gait parameter improvements with similar training.

value.estimand: experimental group change from baseline to 6 weeks
value.uncertainty: Strength training component should improve 5TSTS; variability in baseline function affects magnitude.
value.rationale: Lower extremity strengthening in PD typically reduces 5TSTS time by 2-4 seconds. Program includes targeted strengthening.

value.estimand: experimental group change from baseline to 6 weeks
value.uncertainty: 6MWT responsive to aerobic training; boxing provides moderate-vigorous aerobic stimulus.
value.rationale: Aerobic exercise in PD improves 6MWT by 50-100 feet. Non-contact boxing provides moderate-vigorous intensity aerobic training.

value.estimand: experimental group change from baseline to 6 weeks
value.uncertainty: PDQ39 may not change significantly in short 6-week intervention; physical domain may improve more than total score.
value.rationale: Exercise interventions in PD typically show modest improvements in PDQ39 total score. Short 6-week duration limits magnitude.

value.estimand: experimental group change from baseline to 6 weeks
value.uncertainty: MDS UPDRS motor section may improve slightly with exercise, but 6 weeks insufficient for disease modification.
value.rationale: Exercise may reduce MDS UPDRS motor scores by 2-5 points in short term. Disease progression continues in control group.

analysis_trace.content: NCT06538298: Early phase 1 single-group pilot RCT of multimodal exercise with gamification (non-contact boxing plus SMARTfit) vs waitlist control in Parkinson disease (Hoehn & Yahr 1-3). N=50 estimated, 6-week intervention, 3 days/week, 60 min/session.

Adults 40-80 years with idiopathic PD, Hoehn & Yahr stages 1-3, stable medications 3 months, sedentary (<60 min/week moderate-vigorous exercise), medically cleared. Excludes DBS within 3 months, other neurological disease, current Rock Steady participants.

Multimodal exercise combining aerobic (boxing), balance, strengthening, flexibility with cognitive-motor dual-task training via gamification (SMARTfit). Targets balance, gait, functional strength, and cardiovascular endurance through task-specific training and neuroplasticity.

Primary endpoints assess feasibility (fidelity, adherence, retention, data collection completeness, safety, satisfaction). Secondary endpoints assess efficacy: balance (Mini-BESTest 0-28), gait (FGA 0-30), physical activity (IPAQ minutes), gait speed (10m walk m/s), functional strength (5TSTS seconds), cardiovascular endurance (6MWT feet), QoL (PDQ39), disease severity (MDS UPDRS). Timeframe 21 months for all.

Non-contact boxing supervised by licensed PTs. Risk of falls during balance challenges and boxing movements. Similar interventions show low-to-moderate fall rates with no serious adverse events in supervised settings. Waitlist control has minimal risk.

1) Recruitment challenges limiting power; 2) Attrition in 21-month timeframe exceeding 6-week intervention; 3) Masking absence risks performance bias; 4) Waitlist control contamination; 5) Single-center generalizability limits.

PMC3263544 (Vitorio 2011): 6-month multimodal exercise in PD (n=24) improved gait parameters with good retention. EuropePMC searches show boxing and gamified exercise in PD demonstrate feasibility, adherence rates 75-90%, retention 70-85%, Mini-BESTest improvements 2-4 points, FGA improvements 2-4 points, 6MWT gains 50-100 feet. Evidence supports positive feasibility and modest efficacy signals.

No direct published results for NCT06538298 as of cutoff. Evidence derived from similar PD exercise trials with varying duration (6-24 weeks). Exact gamification protocol (SMARTfit) data limited. Pilot study nature limits precision for efficacy endpoints.
